page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the arm64 AWS Graviton2 processor using the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture. The configuration supplies 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core running at 2.5 GHz, eliminating resource contention from simultaneous multithreading. It includes 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, 32 MB L3 cache, and provides hardware cryptographic acceleration with native AES. Memory is configured at 16.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features also integrate 474 GB of attached NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operating without discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier throughput across multi-core and input/output-sensitive tasks. The system scores 12133.14 on stress-ng multi-core and 5364.0 on Geekbench multi-core, reflecting predictable scaling across its 8 dedicated cores. Memory bandwidth shows robust performance, achieving 473.11 GB/sec cached and 116.89 GB/sec uncached reads. Real-world services exhibit steady metrics, with Redis reaching 9.43 million SET operations per second, PassMark database operations scoring 5269.76, and static web serving recording 9.78 GB/sec throughput. In contrast, single-thread performance trails modern high-frequency designs, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 930.0 and weak decompression throughput on bzip3 and gzip.

The primary tradeoff of the c6gd.2xlarge is its arm64 architecture, requiring software ecosystems to support AArch64 binaries, alongside lower single-threaded compute density compared to x86 counterparts. However, from a cost-efficiency standpoint, the presence of 474 GB of local high-speed NVMe storage and dedicated vCPUs reduces overhead for operations requiring fast scratch space. This profile makes the c6gd.2xlarge an effective deployment target for containerized microservices, distributed caching layers, web serving, software build pipelines, and transactional database workloads that benefit from direct NVMe I/O.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gd.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring an 8-core arm64 AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processor at 2.5 GHz with dedicated physical cores, 16.0 GB of RAM, and 474 GB of integrated NVMe SSD instance storage. Built on the Nitro hypervisor with 2 Gbps baseline networking, it avoids GPU acceleration in favor of efficient CPU and I/O density. Benchmarks demonstrate solid multi-core and memory throughput, including 12133.14 on stress-ng multi-core, 9.43 million Redis SET operations per second, and 9.78 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Single-threaded performance is more modest, posting a Geekbench single-core score of 930.0. The platform delivers cost-efficient performance for distributed caching, multi-threaded CI/CD builds, transactional web services, and database workloads requiring high-speed local scratch disks.
